khaddar: A coarse homespun cotton cloth from India.
khaf: The eleventh letter of the Hebrew and Aramaic alphabets, kaph, especially when pronounced as a fricative (rather than as a plosive).
khaki: A dull, yellowish-brown colour, the colour of dust.
khamsin: A hot, dry wind, common in Egypt, Sudan and the Levant towards the end of March and April, which blows (for about 50 days each year) from the desert, bringing with it hot weathe…
khan: A ruler over various Turkic and Mongol peoples in the Middle Ages.
khanate: The polity ruled by a khan, comprising one or more tribes or clans; a state or dominion ruled by this polity; its territory.
khat: A shrub, Catha edulis, whose leaves are used as a mild stimulant when chewed or brewed as tea; also a drug produced from this plant.
khedive: The title of the hereditary monarch of Egypt from 1805–1914, nominally ruling as a viceroy of the Sultan of Turkey.
khedivial: Of or relating to a khedive.
khi: Alternative spelling of chi (uppercase Χ, lowercase χ), the 22nd letter of the Greek alphabet.
khirkah: The robe or mantle worn by Muslim dervishes.
khoums: A subdivision of the Mauritanian ouguiya.
